materialChanges: Replaced the expected-limit calculation with a prospective operating-probability design: 252 people per group gives about an 80% chance that the lower 95% limit exceeds 5 mg/dL when the true difference is 9 mg/dL under the stated normal approximation; the 3 mg/dL case and downstream funding statement are now probabilistic.

Recast both normal curves as plug-in normal confidence profiles with relative-likelihood axes and explicit warnings that neither the curves nor the shaded confidence intervals describe where future repeat estimates will land.

Calibrated the five interval positions, practice, transfer, assessment feedback and wrap-up so exclusion of zero is model-dependent evidence rather than proof, and threshold values outside an interval are described as outside the reported interval rather than impossible.

Distinguished anchor-based and distribution-based MCID estimation from patient preference elicitation and from a service decision threshold for a between-group effect across the objective, explanation, check, assessment, claims and glossary.

Removed unsupported complication-pathway and individual-category inferences, stated that a group-mean difference does not imply an individual change, and removed the invented study's individual-care recommendation.

Added an explicit plan, symmetry check and self-explanation prompt to the worked example; added the string response "2.28" to the numeric assessment ledger; and calibrated the description of bias without changing the assessed distinction.

reviewDispositions.rationale: Scene 5 now specifies an 80% target, uses 1.96 + z0.80 in the sample-size derivation, rounds 251.2 up to 252 per group, and states the operating probability rather than promising a position. It gives the finite-sample error probability for a true 3 mg/dL effect, gives the separate 1005-per-group design for 80% probability of position B, and scene 8 uses the corrected 252-person funding basis.

Both chart titles, axes, series labels, alt text and long descriptions now identify a plug-in normal confidence profile and relative likelihood. They explicitly deny a repeat-estimate sampling-distribution or probability interpretation and distinguish the observed confidence interval from future estimates.

The five-position table and its applications now use calibrated statements tied to the stated model and confidence procedure. Practice, transfer, assessment summaries and the wrap-up no longer call effects real, proved, demonstrated or settled; they say which values lie inside or outside the reported interval and what evidence supports or leaves open.

The objective, scene 3, glossary, claim ledger and threshold-source assessment now distinguish observed-change-to-anchor MCID estimation, distribution-based information, patient preference elicitation and a prospectively justified service threshold. The 5 mg/dL value is explicitly a service rule, not an MCID, and translating an individual-change MCID into a between-group threshold requires an explicit bridge.

Scene 8 removes the deductions about how many participants exceed or approach 126 mg/dL and whether individuals cross a category. Scenes 1 and 8 now state that the reported 9 mg/dL is a difference between group means and cannot identify individual changes or category crossings without individual-level data and an appropriate model.

The unsupported surrogate and complication-pathway statements were removed from scenes 3 and 8. Scene 8 no longer maps or cites the fasting-glucose diagnostic-range claim, while the supported level-versus-change use remains confined to scene 4 with its existing NIDDK mapping.
The independently confirmed pilot, 60-person, 1200-person, retinal-screening and S/T assessment calculations were retained. The S and T p-values remain stated as both rounding to 0.00007.

The worked example now states a plan before execution, checks that both interval limits are 8.1 mg/dL from the estimate, and asks the learner to explain why excluding zero does not establish that the effect clears the service threshold.

The concrete two-reader opening and natural first-read route were retained. The only opening revision corrects a group-to-individual inference without adding governance vocabulary or weakening the motivating contrast.

The statistical-significance and bias alignment blocks, prior-lesson links and relation values remain intact. Bias wording was calibrated for accuracy while preserving the adopted meaning and the threshold-comparison consequence.

The three-stage fading practice and the retinal-screening transfer with its absolute-versus-relative distractor remain intact. Only the certainty of the reported conclusion was calibrated; the transfer operation and alignment were not weakened.

The S and T arithmetic praised in this note was retained, but the note's endorsement of 123 per group was not retained because the academic review correctly showed that 123 gives only about a 50% chance of clearing the threshold when the true difference is 9 mg/dL. The prospective design now uses 252 per group for the declared 80% target.
The acceptableResponses array for item-lower-limit now includes the JSON string "2.28" while retaining the numeric tolerance and the rounded one-decimal correct answer.

evidenceChecked: All eight scene files retain one level-one heading, logical subordinate headings and manifest-defined reading order; the assessment remains untimed and retakeable with numeric, choice and text routes that do not require drag, hover, sound, motion or personal health data.

Both local chart JSON files retain alt text, detailed outcome-equivalent long descriptions, exact underlying numbers and prose/table alternatives; the revision removes the visually misleading repeat-sampling interpretation and does not rely on colour or position alone.

The new sample-size mathematics uses dollar-delimited LaTeX, defines the target probability and symbols in surrounding prose, preserves units, and supplies a calculator-checkable nonvisual reasoning path.

Static inspection found no raw HTML or entities, Markdown images, scripts, executable code, active SVG, remote embeds, unsafe URL schemes, path traversal, secrets, identifiable learner or patient data, or unlicensed media in the pack.

The cases, services, thresholds and patient are labelled invented; educational and non-clinical boundaries remain visible; unsupported individual and health-outcome inferences and the implied individual-care recommendation were removed.

Every reference retains a permitted source type, ISO date fields, bounded bibliographic fields, factual-reference use, facts-only-original-expression basis, concrete rights evidence and checked-no-agent-restriction-found status; no source is marked human-only.

lesson.json declares CC-BY-4.0, thirdPartyAssets is empty, ATTRIBUTION.md identifies the accountable principal, original pack materials, source uses, access boundaries and lack of third-party assets, and the author and review runs retain disclosed IDs and instruction digests.

Pack-level relational checks found every mapped claim in a same-scene source note with all supporting source IDs, and found valid scene, objective, outcome, rubric, glossary, claim and reference links; all acceptableResponses entries are strings.
limitations: Per the operator's scope restriction, site schemas and the machine-readable quorum policy were not opened and no npm command was run. JSON parsing, identity invariants, field limits, Markdown safety scans, claim-note coverage and internal relationship checks passed, but repository schema/source-preflight/verify checks remain an operator condition.

No rendered browser, keyboard-only session, screen reader, 200% zoom/reflow, reduced-motion, print or non-web export test was available; the audit establishes source-level equivalence and semantics, not empirical assistive-technology behavior.

No source URL, licence page, robots policy or external full text was reopened in this run. The audit relied on the pack's dated access/rights records and the reviews; the academic reviewer reported that some exact PMC paragraphs and locators could not be reopened.

The PR 119 COMMENTED transports and their non-dismissed equivalence were supplied by the operator and were not independently queried. Provenance diversity is disclosed and attested, not verified, and all roles share the same accountable GitHub principal.

rationale: The original candidate is unchanged except for the two committed advisory reviews, and both eligible inputs identify PREM-STA-012 version 0.1.0 at candidate 8bedbff9df9dfd81dee1018ed58a89ead3fec492. They provide exactly one academic and one learning-design input from two declared providers and two distinct run IDs; both request-changes verdicts are eligible under standard-lesson-v3 and do not claim to approve the final edit. This fresh run disposed all thirteen indexed findings, incorporated every blocking academic and learning-design correction, preserved the recalculated values that remained sound, and declined only the learning note's endorsement of the conceptually insufficient 123-person prospective design. The resulting lesson presents a coherent, calibrated distinction among statistical significance, confidence intervals, MCID estimation and service decision thresholds; its assessment and representations now match that model. The source-level accessibility-and-rights audit is satisfied with the stated operational and verification limitations. On that evidence the content decision is merge, subject to replacing the required placeholders, recording the real final content commit, and passing the maintainer-run validation and GitHub provenance gates; this artifact does not itself merge or publish the lesson.
dissent: Both eligible reviewers returned request-changes. Their findings have been dispositioned, but neither reviewer saw or approved the final revision; the fresh finalizer is accountable for it.
The learning-design review declared that github:VSBDev operates authoring, review and finalization runs. Principal-level independence is absent even though the disclosed run IDs and providers differ.

Learning-design finding 4 praised the 123-per-group calculation. That part was not retained because the academic review identified the missing target-probability quantile; the separately praised S and T calculations were retained.
